fields.current_blocker: What is currently preventing the metric from reaching threshold, or null if the SD is implemented and validated
fields.direction: lower_is_better or higher_is_better -- which direction indicates substrate progress
fields.observations: Ordered list of experiments that have produced readings on this metric, annotated with substrate state at the time. Chronological order. Include non-contributory and superseded runs -- the zero-readings and failures are the most informative part of the trajectory.
fields.prediction: Explicit forward hypothesis: given the current trajectory slope and substrate state, what value range should the next experiment produce, and under what conditions? If null, no confident prediction is possible yet.
fields.primary_metric: Name of the key metric this SD should move
fields.primary_metric_description: What it measures and why it is the right quantity
fields.target: Threshold expression the fully-implemented SD must satisfy

metric_trajectory.purpose: Track how the primary test metric for each SD has moved across substrate iterations. Enables predictive hypotheses: given the co-variation of metric value vs substrate state, what should the next experiment produce? The trajectory is more informative than any individual PASS/FAIL because it reveals whether the substrate is the bottleneck or the hypothesis.

node_class.purpose: Per-entry work-graph debt classification (docs/architecture/work_graph_debt_vocabulary.md). Makes an entry's KIND machine-readable so a 'gated on X' phrase in implementation_hint / status prose can be validated against it, and so the /governance recommendation sweep can order discovery-debt ahead of execution backlog (prefer-discovery-debt = the EFE epistemic-value term on the work graph).
node_class.value_note: The bracket is PART of the token -- write it verbatim, never the bare word. puzzle/mystery are the two sub-kinds of complex (probe-gated); a complex (probe-gated) entry MAY be refined to puzzle (known rules) or mystery (known data) once the probe's shape is known.
node_class.default_reading: A substrate_queue entry is by construction the execution backlog for /implement-substrate -- an UNMARKED entry is read as complicated (buildable) (build it). Mark node_class explicitly only when the entry's residual is actually a reducible unknown: complex (probe-gated) when what is owed is a spike (a REE diagnostic), not a build; aleatoric (irreducible) when the residual is real noise to robustify against, not research. A complex (probe-gated) entry usually should not be a naked build task -- surface it to the /governance sweep first.
node_class.gated_on_rule: Any 'gated on X' / 'gated_on' phrase in an entry's implementation_hint or status prose is well-formed only if X resolves to one of allowed_values (or names a concrete upstream node that itself carries one). verify_governance_cycle.py check I flags a 'gated on' phrase whose entry has no valid node_class.
node_class.populated_by: /governance Step 6a (6a-iii schema write + 6a-iv autopsy create) sets node_class on every new / updated entry; historical (pre-2026-07-10) entries may lack it and are read under default_reading until a governance cycle next touches them.

severity.purpose: Whether this entry's defect is dangerous to keep running NEW, unrelated experiments against while it is still open -- orthogonal to node_class (can we build the fix) and priority (how urgently should we build it). Design: evidence/planning/substrate_defect_gate_plan_2026-08-07.md.
severity.value_note: corrupting = produces evidence that looks valid but isn't (silent) -- forward: new experiments touching substrate_paths should be BLOCKED, not just warned (see /queue-experiment Step 2.5c). degrading = known limitation; weakens confidence but doesn't invalidate outright -- forward: WARN, don't block. cosmetic = no evidence impact (a lint gap, a naming issue, dead code) -- no gate.
severity.default_reading: Most substrate_queue entries are ordinary missing-feature backlog with no evidence-corruption risk -- an UNMARKED entry is read as the implicit fourth bucket 'not-yet-run' (nothing has been tested against it yet, so there is nothing to gate on) and Step 2.5c takes no action on it. Only stamp severity when the entry names substrate that ALREADY-RUN or FUTURE experiments could silently corrupt.
severity.populated_by: /failure-autopsy Step 7, at the same point recommended_substrate_queue_entry is filled (the autopsy has already diagnosed the defect, so classifying its danger is nearly free there). /governance Step 6a-iii/6a-iv persists it into substrate_queue.json unchanged -- governance does not re-derive severity from scratch.
severity.backfill_note: The 145 pre-2026-08-07 entries were deliberately NOT backfilled (see the plan doc's 'explicitly out of scope' section) -- most are complicated (buildable) backlog with no evidence-corruption risk, so a blanket sweep was judged wasted effort. Fill going forward; backfill retroactively only for an entry whose failure_record suggests a corrupting-severity defect.

substrate_paths.purpose: Repo-relative path(s) (relative to ree-v3/) the defect actually lives in or corrupts -- makes an entry queryable by CODE FOOTPRINT instead of only by claim. Distinct from unblocks_claims, which answers 'which claims does fixing this help'; substrate_paths answers 'what does a NEW, possibly-unrelated experiment need to avoid touching while this is open'. Design: evidence/planning/substrate_defect_gate_plan_2026-08-07.md.
substrate_paths.format: A list of strings, each either a bare file path (e.g. "ree_core/predictors/e3_selector.py") or a file path plus a function name separated by '::' when the defect is scoped to one function (e.g. "ree_core/predictors/e3_selector.py::compute_harm_cost_fallback"). Matching in /queue-experiment Step 2.5c and check_substrate_path_overlap.py is at MODULE granularity (the '::function' suffix narrows the human-readable description of where the defect lives, but does not narrow which experiments are flagged).
substrate_paths.default_reading: Absent/empty on an entry means the defect has no known code footprint yet (or is a pure documentation/process gap) -- Step 2.5c and check_substrate_path_overlap.py take no action on such an entry regardless of severity.
substrate_paths.populated_by: /failure-autopsy Step 7 -- filled at the same point as severity, because the autopsy has already read the source to diagnose the failure, so naming the path(s) is nearly free there and far more reliable than reconstructing it later from prose.

status_phase.purpose: Machine-checkable one-token phase for an entry, ALONGSIDE the free-text `status` narrative log -- status stays exactly as-is (it is a genuinely useful changelog, not noise) and is never replaced or truncated. Exists because `status` is already parsed by tooling via ad hoc regex/substring matching against a free-running snake_case narrative string (generate_inter_governance_workset.py _status_resolved/_status_terminal/_status_implementation_complete/_substrate_resolved; verify_governance_cycle.py's 'gated on' check; substrate_queue_writeback_drift.py's field_disagreement check) -- which is both unreadable to a human scanning many entries at once and fragile enough that `ready` already has to override it (a past status-string-only false positive is the documented reason `ready` is authoritative and status a secondary hint). status_phase gives both audiences a stable, greppable field without touching the narrative.
status_phase.value_note: probe_gated = the residual is a REE diagnostic/spike, not a build (mirrors node_class complex (probe-gated)). build_owed = a concrete buildable lever is named but not yet built (mirrors node_class complicated (buildable)). validation_pending = the needed build(s) are done (BUILT and/or PROMOTED) and what remains is an experiment run/result, not construction. route_exhausted = every currently-known lever on this route has been tried and refuted; forward motion needs a new route, not another letter on this one. closed = ready:true and no unresolved dependents.
status_phase.default_reading: Absent on historical entries -- infer conservatively rather than assume: probe_gated if ready:false and node_class is complex (probe-gated) or unset; build_owed if ready:false and depends_on_unresolved names a lever not yet built; validation_pending if ready:false and every fallback_ladder/depends_on item is BUILT/VALIDATED with only run results outstanding; closed if ready:true.
status_phase.populated_by: /governance Step 6a-iii/6a-iv, same population point as node_class/severity/substrate_paths -- set on every new/updated entry going forward. Historical entries populated opportunistically when a cycle next touches them, not backfilled in bulk (same posture as severity's backfill_note below).

failure_record[].resolved.purpose: Per-item resolution state for one entry in a `failure_record` list, so a reader (or script) can tell which of a long failure_record history are still live open questions vs later superseded/addressed, without parsing the free-text `metric`/`target`/`addressed_by` prose on every item. The existing sub-fields (run_id, experiment_type, metric, target, and the informal addressed_by/adjudication/source_autopsy prose already present on some historical items) are unchanged -- this adds one more optional key per item.
failure_record[].resolved.value_note: open = still the live characterisation of an unaddressed gap. resolved = a later build/lever directly closed this specific failure mode (name the resolving run_id/session in the item's own addressed_by text). superseded = a later, more specific experiment on the same question replaced this item's read without anything being 'fixed' -- e.g. an isolation run overturning an earlier marginal/confounded read.
failure_record[].resolved.default_reading: Absent means open -- do not read a missing field as resolved.
failure_record[].resolved.populated_by: /failure-autopsy Step 7, when the autopsy's own finding resolves or supersedes a specific prior failure_record item on the SAME entry (uncommon -- most autopsies add a new item rather than resolve an old one), and /governance Step 6a-iii, the more common path: a later build's validation run makes an earlier failure_record item's `target` moot. Not backfilled across historical entries in bulk; populate going forward and opportunistically when reading an old entry closely enough to judge each item confidently.

failure_record[].run_role.purpose: Whether a failure_record item's `run_id` names a run that executed AGAINST the substrate this entry describes (post_build) or one that CHARACTERISED the gap the build was meant to close (pre_build). Added 2026-08-15 (FM11d) because generate_inter_governance_workset._substrate_landing_cutoff dates the substrate landing from these run stamps, and had no way to tell the two apart -- it read every one as post-build validation. Measured on this corpus at the time: of the 97 items datable against their own entry's implemented_utc, 37 (38%) PREDATE it. A pre-build stamp used as a landing bound sets the retest cutoff below the true landing, so stale pre-substrate evidence satisfies 'a retest has run since the substrate landed' -- a wrong HOLD that silently tells /governance a retest happened when it did not.
failure_record[].run_role.value_note: post_build = the substrate existed when this run executed, so the run stamp is a usable UPPER bound on the landing instant, AND the run itself counts as post-substrate evidence (the generator's coverage test is at-or-after such a cutoff, not strictly after -- otherwise the run sets the bar and then fails it). pre_build = the run predates the build; it is NOT a landing bound. unknown = cannot be established (no parseable run stamp, or nothing dates the entry's landing).
failure_record[].run_role.default_reading: ABSENT reads as `unknown`, NOT as post_build -- the opposite of the pre-2026-08-15 behaviour, and deliberately so. Only an explicit post_build raises the landing cutoff, so an unbackfilled item cannot silently move it.
failure_record[].run_role.phased_builds: An entry that landed in PHASES needs `substrate_built_utc` on the individual item, which overrides everything: SD-035's v3_exq_894a postdates the 2026-04-21 BLA/CeA landing but predates the 2026-08-09 trainable-attribution-head build it motivated, and only the per-item stamp can say so. Set `substrate_built_utc` when adding a failure_record item to a multi-phase entry.
failure_record[].run_role.populated_by: scripts/backfill_failure_record_run_role.py backfilled all 281 items 2026-08-15 and records its per-item derivation in the sibling `run_role_basis` field (re-runnable; `--apply` to write). /failure-autopsy Step 7 and /governance Step 6a-iii should set it explicitly on any NEW failure_record item -- an autopsy's own gap-characterisation run is pre_build; a validation run queued after a build lands is post_build.

metric_trajectory.current_blocker: SD-022 substrate not active during EXQ-323. When z_harm_a derives from the same 50-dim proximity EMA as z_harm_s, the nonredundancy objective is applied to a pair of representations that share their information source. The training signal is therefore unstable: any reduction in cosine similarity achieved in one episode can be reversed when the proximity geometry changes. SD-022 (limb_damage_enabled=True) provides a causally independent information source for z_harm_a (body damage state), giving the nonredundancy objective a genuine basis for stable disentanglement.

queue.clamp_ordering_constraint_2026_07_21: BINDING CONSTRAINT ON THIS EXTENSION (fixed in ree-v3 2026-07-21, session silly-hellman-f0808b). StructuredCuriosity.compute_score_bias clamps to +/-curiosity_bias_scale, and BEFORE this fix that clamp was applied to the SUM of all three sub-flavours -- with 314b/314c contributing UNIFORM torch.ones(K) broadcasts. Once w_unc*unc + w_lp*lp >= curiosity_bias_scale every element pinned to the rail, the returned tensor became exactly uniform, and the per-candidate 314a component was ANNIHILATED. A uniform vector is argmin-invariant at the E3 commit point (e3_selector.py:3113, and :3022 under use_f_eligibility_demotion), so curiosity went behaviourally silent with no diagnostic saying so, and its authority was NON-MONOTONE in the configured weights (raising them drove the system INTO saturation). Reproduced as a unit mutation check: pre-fix the returned bias is tensor([-0.1]*5) and the per-candidate range is identically 0.0 across an 8x novelty-weight sweep -- the V3-EXQ-667 '4x byte-identical to 2x' readiness signature. FIX: the accumulated bias is decomposed into the argmin-INERT uniform offset (total.mean(), carrying 314b/314c) and the argmin-RELEVANT per-candidate deviation, and each is clamped SEPARATELY -- so the clamp bounds curiosity's selection-relevant influence at bias_scale (original intent preserved) and its total magnitude at 2*bias_scale, while a large uniform sub-signal can no longer flatten the ranking. WHAT THE 314b/314c PER-CANDIDATE EXTENSION MUST KNOW: the clamp now bounds a DECOMPOSITION, not the raw sum. When 314b/314c become genuine per-candidate vectors they will contribute to the DEVIATION term rather than only the offset, so all three sub-flavours will then compete for the same +/-bias_scale argmin-relevant budget. The extension must therefore decide how that budget is shared (e.g. per-sub-flavour deviation clamps, or a raised bias_scale) or it will ship still able to rail the ranking -- the same defect one layer down. NEW DIAGNOSTICS to gate on at readiness (StructuredCuriosity.get_state): last_clamp_saturated_frac (fraction of candidates whose deviation is pinned at the rail; its ceiling is (K-1)/K, not 1.0, because the deviation is zero-mean -- that property is exactly why the clamp can no longer flatten the vector completely) and last_bias_range (surviving argmin-relevant span). Assert last_bias_range > 0 and last_clamp_saturated_frac below its ceiling BEFORE scoring any curiosity-dependent DV, rather than discovering a vacuous channel in a null result (the 604a / 624a / 614d / 640a failure class). Contracts: ree-v3 tests/contracts/test_mech_314_curiosity_clamp_ordering.py (S1-S5, mutation-checked against the pre-fix clamp). Trace of record: REE_assembly e85ff72f74, node infant_substrate:GAP-14 key governance_2026_07_21b. SUBSTRATE FIX ONLY -- status/ready UNCHANGED, no claims.yaml edit, no experiment queued.

(b) Still-open foraging-competence half (634): strengthen/lengthen P0/P1 so >=2/3 seeds reach self-sustaining consumption (only seed 43 survives P1). (c) Test-design: redefine the mature-test z_goal acceptance readout to read AT genuine consumption events (632-style num_contact_events) rather than the forced-feed-calibrated frozen-peak G3>0.4, which is anti-correlated with foraging. occupancy_gap_diagnosis_2026_08_12.summary: Diagnosed WHY fraction_in_external_task stayed exactly 0.0 on every seed/arm of both 464d and 467d despite the 2026-06-13 drive landing. TWO independent, compounding root causes, both empirically confirmed by instrumented replay of the actual driver code (dry-run budgets, seed 42): (1) DRIVER BUG (not a substrate defect): _clone_for_arm() in both v3_exq_464d and v3_exq_467d clones the trained agent via REEAgent.state_dict()/load_state_dict() only. GoalState is a plain Python object (not nn.Module), so its cross-episode z_goal attractor is invisible to state_dict() and is silently dropped on clone -- the eval clone's goal_state.is_active() is False for the entire eval, hard-gating external_task_drive's engagement to 0.0 regardless of beta_elevated or goal_proximity (external_task_drive_require_goal_active=True by default). Confirmed: post-training agent had goal_state.is_active()=True (goal_norm=0.49); the naive clone had is_active()=False (goal_norm=0.0); patching the clone with agent.goal_state.load_state_dict(agent.goal_state.state_dict()) restored is_active()=True and made external_task_drive read 0.30-0.48 instead of exactly 0.0 on every tick. (2) SUBSTRATE MAGNITUDE MISMATCH (fixed here): even with (1) fixed, dacc_pe (uncapped by default, dacc_pe_cap=None) measured ~15-17 throughout eval -- two orders of magnitude above external_task's max affinity-logit contribution (bias 1.0 + engagement<=1.0 * affinity_weight, typically <=5) -- so internal_planning's argmax never yielded to external_task regardless of engagement, and the coordinator's soft-weighted mode vector (module docstring: 'Soft-weighted, NOT one-hot') collapsed to one-hot internal_planning on every tick. Fixed by adding SalienceCoordinatorConfig.affinity_input_cap (None default, bit-identical) which clamps each AFFINITY signal (not salience_aggregate) to [-cap, cap] before its per-mode weight is applied -- wired through REEConfig as salience_affinity_input_cap (3-site from_dims plumbing) -> agent.py's sal_cfg construction -> SalienceCoordinator.tick()'s logits loop. VERIFIED TOGETHER: with both fixes applied in a scratch diagnostic (goal_state clone fix + affinity_input_cap=2.0), the SAME seed/config that previously read fraction_in_external_task=0.0 on both arms now reads ARM_ASYM_STICKY_TASK=1.0 (n_switches=0, sticky over-binding) vs ARM_SYMMETRIC=0.3 (n_switches=2, genuine competition) -- i.e. C1 (asym occupancy >= sym + 0.10 margin) and C2 (asym switches <= sym switches) BOTH pass on this seed, the exact MECH-266 over-binding signature the experiment is designed to detect, with no saturation degeneracy (not the 464b 100%-always problem: the symmetric arm still shows genuine switching).

cap_calibration_probe_2026_08_13.summary: Answers implementation_hint_update_2026_08_13's H1-vs-H2 question with a synthetic probe against the REAL SalienceCoordinator/SalienceCoordinatorConfig classes (not a full curriculum re-run -- that is /queue-experiment territory and REFUSED by the autopsy's re-derive brake as a naked letter re-queue). Two probes, not committed to the repo (scratch only): (1) single-tick softmax sweep of affinity_input_cap in [0.25..20.0] against dacc_pe=16.0 (the diagnosed magnitude) and both engagement sub-regimes; (2) a 400-tick stateful sim of SalienceCoordinator.tick() with a crude beta_gate commit/release duty cycle, sweeping affinity_input_cap x hysteresis ratio. FINDING (H1 supported, H2 NOT the primary cause): the single-tick operating_mode['external_task'] IS genuinely graded across cap ~0.25-2.0 and responds continuously to goal_proximity when the engagement commit term is not saturating -- the softmax/argmax representation is NOT structurally incapable of grading. At cap=2.0 (the value 464e/467e actually used), the STATEFUL sim reproduces the observed step-function shape almost exactly (frac_ext=1.0 at the sticky ratio, then 0.0 with a single settle-switch at every looser ratio) -- i.e. cap=2.0 itself is very plausibly the miscalibration, not a structural ceiling. At cap=1.0-1.5, the SAME sim produces a genuinely mixed, dynamic regime (frac_ext=0.6965-0.9705 with 5-83 real switches per 400-tick run, not 0 or n_episodes) -- direct synthetic evidence that a mixed regime IS reachable at SOME cap. SECOND, independent finding read directly from agent.py:6890 (not from the probe): external_task_drive's engagement formula (config.py:3016-3018) is `clip(commit_w*float(beta_gate.is_elevated) + prox_w*goal_proximity, 0, 1)` -- `beta_gate.is_elevated` is a hard boolean commitment LATCH (MECH-090, ree_core/heartbeat/beta_gate.py -- 'beta as a commitment gate, not a learning gate', by design), and at the default commit_weight=1.0 ANY elevation alone saturates engagement to exactly 1.0 regardless of proximity. This is a genuine STRUCTURAL discreteness source INDEPENDENT of affinity_input_cap -- no cap value can smooth it, since the cap only bounds the AFFINITY LOGIT after engagement is already computed. Combined with the mode-switch mechanism itself being a Schmitt trigger by design (SD-032a: 'Mode transitions are discrete, not graded'), the corrected reading is: H1 and H2 are NOT mutually exclusive as the autopsy framed them -- the underlying soft signal is graded (H1-favourable, recalibration is worth doing), but the DISCRETE occupancy-fraction/switch-count statistics 464e/467e measure are inherently coarse readouts of a latched, hysteretic state machine and will show step-like behaviour for SOME parameter settings by design, independent of cap tuning. RECOMMENDATION for the next real (non-refused) H1 cap-sweep experiment: (i) sweep affinity_input_cap densely in [0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75] rather than re-testing 2.0 or blindly widening the range -- this is the band where the synthetic model shows real switching dynamics; (ii) additionally instrument operating_mode['external_task'] (the continuous pre-argmax value) per tick, not only the discrete occupancy fraction, per H2's own probe design in the autopsy -- the synthetic probe here is a toy model (crude random-walk commit duty cycle, single dacc_foraging/difficulty setting) and does not substitute for measuring the real substrate's actual duty cycle and dACC magnitudes.

This is the MEASUREMENT prerequisite shared by ALL FOUR retention legs of the competence_floor question (portfolio 2026-07-18 section 53: 'Every leg MUST record the post-installation competence trajectory'). It is INSTRUMENTATION ONLY -- it changes no update rule and is orthogonal to the three manipulation nodes (mech457_distributional_critic, mech457_bc_aux_schedule, mech457_policy_kl_anchor). WHY THIS IS BLOCKING RATHER THAN COSMETIC. The two retention legs whose manipulations landed 2026-07-18 cannot be queued honestly without this: their measurement_requirement mandates the post-installation competence TRAJECTORY, and terminal-only measurement is exactly what kept the retention deficit invisible for ten legs (V3-EXQ-780 is the worked failure). Queueing them against a terminal DV would reproduce that failure and enter a retention verdict into the frozen ledger on a test that never measured retention. Corroboration that nothing exists: all 18 mech457 experiment scripts call capability_eval.evaluate_seed only 1-3 times, always terminal (780 uses 2 = post-BC + terminal).

NOTHING OF THIS EXISTS. Zero hits for eval_every / checkpoint_every / eval_callback / on_episode / probe_callback / ep_offset / start_episode / global_ep across experiments/_lib/ and ree_core/action_learning/. train_a2c (experiments/_lib/mech457_explorer_classes.py:546-565) exposes 16 optional parameters and EVERY one is a reward/loss-shaping hook (intrinsic, mode_gate, credit_replay, archive, coef_schedule, entropy_schedule, bc_demo, bc_aux_schedule, approach_drive); none is an observation hook. Its guard dict (:795-804) returns rolling-window MEANS only (mean_train_forage_recent et al) -- no per-episode series, no resumable state. train_bootstrap_explorer (experiments/_lib/mech457_bootstrap_explorer.py:259-263) is a thin wrapper that builds the schedules and delegates; it adds no hook and no offset. The ep_offset identifier DOES appear in several driver scripts (v3_exq_732a:530,601; v3_exq_718:376; v3_exq_701c:458; v3_exq_324a:186) but purely as a print-progress counter -- it has never been plumbed into a schedule.

WHY DRIVER-SIDE CHUNKING IS NOT AN ACCEPTABLE WORKAROUND (this is the load-bearing finding; do not 'simplify' the build back to it). Segmenting the RL budget into train_a2c calls and evaluating between segments is unfaithful on two independent grounds. (a) SCHEDULES RESTART: coef_schedule/entropy_schedule/bc_aux_schedule are invoked as fn(ep, n_episodes) at mech457_explorer_classes.py:655,659,665 with ep the LOCAL index from `for ep in range(n_episodes)` (:615), and warm_then_anneal / linear_anneal (mech457_bootstrap_explorer.py:231-256) compute warm_cut and span from that same local n_episodes -- so N segments restart the warm-start phase and the anneal N times. Note `denom` does NOT help: it is print-progress only (:786), not schedule input. For H-retention-auxiliary-decay this is fatal in a specific way -- the bc_aux anneal IS the independent variable, so chunking would destroy the manipulation itself. (b) OPTIMISER/NORMALISER STATE RESETS: the Adam optimiser (:600), the _RunningStd reward normaliser (:601), the novelty_counter (:602) and the rolling deques (:603-606) are all constructed as locals immediately before the episode loop, so each segment resets Adam moment estimates, the reward normalisation statistics and count-based novelty. Across a 3000-episode run at a ~250-episode probe cadence that is ~12 resets of precisely the learning dynamics whose erosion is the dependent variable.

WHAT TO BUILD. (1) An observation hook on train_a2c: `probe_every: Optional[int] = None` + `probe_fn: Optional[Callable[[int], Dict[str, Any]]] = None`, both defaulting to None so the OFF path is byte-identical (the established backward-compat pattern in this family -- see the bc_aux_schedule and coef_schedule builds). Fire probe_fn(ep) every probe_every episodes at an episode boundary, collect results into a list, and return it in the guard dict as `competence_trajectory: [{'episode': int, 'foraging_competence': float}, ...]`. (2) Passthrough on BootstrapExplorerConfig (a declared field in as_slice(), like bc_aux_coef_end/bc_aux_anneal_fraction) and on train_bootstrap_explorer. (3) RNG ISOLATION -- THE SUBTLE CORRECTNESS TRAP: the probe runs rollout episodes, so unless the training RNG stream is saved and restored around each probe call, the probe SHIFTS the training rollouts and a probed run silently diverges from an unprobed one. Snapshot and restore torch/numpy/random state around the probe (or give the probe its own dedicated generator), and evaluate on a SEPARATE env instance -- never the training env, whose episode state would be clobbered. (4) The probe must not touch the optimiser, _RunningStd, novelty_counter or the deques.

SAME-STATISTIC REQUIREMENT (non-negotiable). The probe must report the SAME statistic the verdict routes on: unshaped foraging_competence via capability_eval.evaluate_seed:368, which is the statistic post_bc_foraging_competence uses and the one every reference band is denominated in (floor 1.0 / RND plateau 5.22 / lift target 13.05 / the 20.933 install positive control / BC-expert 32.72 / local_view_greedy 48.05). Do NOT substitute the cheaper mean_train_forage_recent: that is SHAPED on-policy training forage measured under the intrinsic drive, is not comparable to those bands, and would put the half-life on a different statistic from the criterion -- the V3-EXQ-643 magnitude-vs-range mismatch class, where a readiness check asserts a different quantity than the criterion consumes.

ACCEPTANCE TEST (the contract that makes the trajectory trustworthy): MEASUREMENT NEUTRALITY. For a fixed seed, a run with the probe ON must produce a BIT-IDENTICAL training trajectory and terminal readout to the same run with the probe OFF -- the probe may only ADD outputs, never perturb. A contract test asserting this (probe-on vs probe-off terminal foraging_competence bit-identical) is the regression that keeps a future edit from quietly making the instrument interact with the experiment. Also assert the trajectory has the expected length (n_episodes // probe_every) and that OFF defaults leave the full existing suite green.

IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE -- HOOK RECOMMENDED OVER MIRRORED LOOP. There is a local precedent for the alternative: experiments/_lib/mech459_probe_r.py:1-24 mirrored the training loop into a separate module rather than adding a hook, and its docstring gives the reason -- a default-None hook still changes the bytes of mech457_explorer_classes.py and therefore the arm_fingerprint substrate_hash of the then-live 780/781. Expect and accept that this edit refuses pre-change baseline arm fingerprints for reuse.

ANTI-ALIAS CONSTRAINT. This node is INSTRUMENTATION ONLY. It must change no update rule, no loss term, no schedule and no value estimator -- otherwise it contaminates the three-way anti-alias the retention portfolio depends on (value estimator only = mech457_distributional_critic / update constraint only = mech457_policy_kl_anchor / auxiliary persistence only = mech457_bc_aux_schedule). queue.implementation_hint: arm_cell computes substrate_hash by hashing source files from disk at cell entry, but the cell executes in-memory bytecode frozen at process start (sys.modules). When the checkout moves mid-run the manifest records the DISK state -- a FALSE-HIT channel, the one failure mode arm_fingerprint.py:20-27's governing asymmetry says must never occur (over-inclusion is supposed to buy false MISSES only). Fix: resolve substrate identity ONCE at process start and reuse it for every cell, rather than a fresh per-cell disk read. Cheap adjunct: re-hash at process exit and stamp a substrate_stable_across_run boolean so a mid-run checkout move is recorded as the instrument event it is, rather than as per-cell substrate identity.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-20, ree-v3 a23f189 (origin/main). Entry created retrospectively 2026-07-20 by session vibrant-chatelet-e113d0: the autopsy recommended `create` but the build landed before any queue entry existed, so this is filed at status implemented / ready false, NOT as open work.

INSTRUMENTATION ONLY -- experiments/_lib/arm_fingerprint.py, manifest_core.py, arm_reuse.py. No ree_core change, no config param, no behavioural effect on any experiment; nothing here can move a metric.

WHAT LANDED, three parts. (1) resolve_substrate_identity() memoises the substrate hash for the process lifetime, keyed by (repo_root, declared scope, extra paths), and compute_arm_fingerprint serves every cell from that one snapshot; first resolution happens at the first cell, after the driver's module-scope imports have frozen the executed bytecode, so recorded identity IS executed identity by construction (driver_script_hash frozen the same way). (2) substrate_stability_report() re-hashes from disk at stamp time and stamp_recording_core writes a top-level substrate_stable_across_run bool (+ substrate_stability_detail when False); two tests, each of which can only prove INSTABILITY -- per-cell hash cardinality > 1, or process snapshot != disk -- catching the one residual the freeze cannot, a module imported lazily after the first cell. Deliberately NOT added to ALWAYS_CORE_KEYS: the pre-2026-07-20 corpus cannot carry it and making it core would WARN on every legacy manifest. (3) arm_reuse.source_run_substrate_unstable() + REFUSE_SUBSTRATE_UNSTABLE refuses to serve any cell out of a run whose cells disagree about their substrate. That is the RETROACTIVE handling of the 42 sweep-flagged runs, done in the lookup path -- completed manifests were NOT edited (completed runs are re-adjudicated by autopsy, never rewritten). Absence of substrate_stable_across_run is not read as instability (that would refuse every banked mint); it falls through to the cardinality test.

Not a hard cut: on a stable run the emitted hash is byte-identical to before, so every banked fingerprint still matches.

SCOPE OF THE CLAIM -- do not repeat the uncorrected headline. intra_run_substrate_divergence_sweep_2026-07-20.md's '42 of 164 (25.6%)' counts runs whose RECORDED HASH VALUE changed, NOT runs that lost experimental control, and must not be cited as the latter (failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-782 and the sweep author's own 2026-07-20T07:30Z WORKSPACE_STATE correction, session zen-dijkstra-c0fe33). _SUBSTRATE_GLOBS is uniformly wider than what any run imports, so an unrelated parallel edit moves the hash without touching the run; on 782 the closure-restricted hash was byte-identical across all four bands. 778a's own confound was likewise REFUTED -- all 8 seeds provably executed one build. What STANDS is the INSTRUMENT defect this node fixes: recorded identity was never guaranteed to be executed identity.

KNOWN OVER-REFUSAL, and why it is correct here. Cardinality > 1 over-reports (driver_script_in_substrate_hash toggled mid-run on one corpus run, V3-EXQ-788; and the over-wide globs). 782 warns that a whole-glob divergence flag would institutionalise that false positive as a standing warning -- but that caution governs a signal that ADJUDICATES SCIENCE, where a false positive wrongly impeaches a real result. The reuse gate has the opposite asymmetry (a false MISS costs compute, a false HIT corrupts a conclusion), so over-refusal is correct HERE precisely because it is wrong THERE; the two must not be collapsed. substrate_stable_across_run is scoped as an INSTRUMENT event, never a confound verdict, and nothing adjudicates a claim off it. 782's secondary routing (closure-restricted recomputation) should narrow both when it lands.

Also corrected: _hoist_multi_arm_substrate_hash's docstring asserted 'all arms of one run execute against the same substrate', which the sweep falsified; the hoist kept only the first hash and so actively HID divergence at the top level. Behaviour unchanged (back-compat), premise documented, per-cell set now exposed via multi_arm_substrate_hashes().

VALIDATION: no EXQ -- this changes no mechanism and gates no claim. Verified by 17 contracts in ree-v3 tests/contracts/test_arm_fingerprint_executed_substrate.py, which encode the failure record's acceptance target directly.

queue.collapse_decision: DO NOT COLLAPSE -- decided 2026-07-22 by session inspiring-perlman-81affd, re-deciding (not inheriting) the deferral by gracious-austin-6eb2ae. The implementation_note's aside that x728b 'defines its own copy' read as residual debt; on inspection it is deliberate design and collapsing it would be net-negative. FOUR REASONS, each verified. (1) THE STATED PURPOSE IS ALREADY DELIVERED, without a refactor: ree-v3/tests/contracts/test_zworld_p0_adoption_reaches_every_driver.py C1 asserts BOTH definition sites import and call the shared run_zworld_p0 (anti-fork), and C2 asserts each sets ZWORLD_P0_EPISODES > 0. So 'a future encoder-warmup change cannot reach some drivers and not others' now fails at commit time. The refactor would buy a property the corpus already holds. (2) x728b's DUPLICATION IS INTENTIONAL INSULATION, NOT DRIFT. It vendors x724's whole training toolkit -- _obs_harm/_obs_harm_a/_obs_harm_history/_e2_contrastive_step/_consumed_summaries/_lpfc_reinforce_loss/_ofc_deval_reinforce_loss plus the constants -- and imports x724 nowhere; its header records the vendoring ('Sourced config ... from V3-EXQ-714 ARM_ON via V3-EXQ-724/727'). x734 does the opposite and delegates to x724. EXPERIMENT_PURPOSE='baseline': a banked-arm baseline WANTS its recipe frozen against upstream drift, so re-coupling it to a shared mutable path inverts its design intent. (3) THE MEASURED DIVERGENCE IS SMALLER THAN 28% BUT POINTS THE SAME WAY. Every training-relevant constant is value-identical between x728b's local copies and x724 (E2_CONTRASTIVE_LR 1e-3, LR_LPFC_BIAS 5e-4, LR_OFC_DEVAL 2e-3, TRANSITION_BUFFER_MAX 256, EMA_DECAY 0.9, OUTCOME_BUF_MAX 512, E2_TRAIN_IN_P1 False, ...), so most of the 62-line diff is the x724.CONST-vs-bare-CONST namespace route rather than behaviour. What genuinely differs is signature and env construction (x734 is rung-based and takes train_env + zworld_p0_env + rung_id + total_denominator; x728b builds _make_env(seed) internally), the warmup label, and print cadence (%50 vs %25). A collapse would therefore merge two bodies that agree on the recipe but disagree on exactly the part -- ownership of env construction -- that a shared function cannot own. (4) IT WOULD BUST A LIVE PASS FOR NOTHING. x728b calls arm_cell(script_path=Path(__file__)) with include_driver_script_in_hash defaulting True, so the driver file is folded into substrate_hash; editing its training path invalidates the banked arms of run v3_exq_728b_trained_allon_capability_point_20260721T113845Z_v3 (PASS, guard green, arm_green=true), one of the three runs this row's own validation_status rests on. Cost side: ree-v3 has no branch CI for the code plane, so the merge gate is a ~6min cloud suite run via scripts/remote_pytest.sh -- real cost against zero property gain. THIS CLOSES THE QUESTION; do not re-open it as generic de-duplication. A SEPARATE AND REAL DEFECT WAS FOUND WHILE DECIDING and is chipped rather than fixed here (it touches ree-v3/experiments/_lib/, under an active claim by interesting-tu-f726f1 at 2026-07-22T18:00Z): x734._train_all_on_agent is executed by reuse-eligible baselines -- v3_exq_742 and the 742m mint both pass include_driver_script_in_hash=False, which is MANDATORY for cross-driver reuse -- yet experiments/v3_exq_734_*.py is in NO substrate-hash glob. _SUBSTRATE_GLOBS is ('ree_core/**/*.py','experiments/_harness.py','experiments/_metrics.py','experiments/_lib/**/*.py'), and a driver file enters a hash only as the calling script's own path, which those two exclude by design. So an edit to the shared training function is INVISIBLE to their fingerprints and can produce a false cache HIT -- reusing a banked arm computed by different training code, the unsafe direction the module documents (over-inclusion -> false misses only). Note this is the opposite of a reason to leave things alone: moving ONLY x734's shared definition into experiments/_lib/ would close it, and would not touch x728b at all. That is a targeted soundness fix, not the symmetric collapse this row asked for, and should be decided on its own evidence.

If that regime is rare or never occurs in practice, this is aleatoric (irreducible) for the current substrate and needs no fix; if it occurs routinely, a companion fix (an 'unexpired commitment, skip re-selection' short-circuit in the E3-tick branch) would need its own design review given its architectural significance (affects E3's core deliberation cadence, not a small mirror-an-existing-pattern diff).

queue.title: MECH-122 sensory-gating half: determine whether/how external sensory input needs to be blocked from reaching z_self/z_world encoders during SWS/REM offline consolidation windows
queue.implementation_hint: MECH-122 bundles two distinct mechanisms: content packaging (has a V3 proxy -- ThetaBuffer.consolidation_summary()/set_consolidation_mode(), ree_core/latent/theta_buffer.py -- never wired into the real sleep pipeline) and sensory gating (suppressing external sensory input during the consolidation window so waking observations cannot interrupt or contaminate it). Sensory gating has ZERO V3 code anywhere in ree_core -- no gate/gating/sensory/spindle-window mechanism of any kind (confirmed by targeted grep, IGW-20260801-226 drafting pass, 2026-08-01). This entry is deliberately node_class complex (probe-gated), not complicated (buildable): SleepLoopManager (ree_core/sleep/phase_manager.py) already runs sleep cycles at episode boundaries via notify_episode_end/run_sleep_cycle, strictly between env.step() calls, not interleaved with them -- so it is NOT YET ESTABLISHED whether waking observations can actually leak into z_self/z_world encoders during an active offline phase under the current architecture, or whether the episode-boundary design already satisfies the biological claim's protective intent by construction (in which case the gap is a missing regression test + claims.yaml documentation update, not new gating code). The probe owed before this can become complicated (buildable): trace whether any code path calls the waking-mode z_self/z_world encoding step while agent.sleep_state indicates an active SWS_ANALOG/REM_ANALOG phase, and if so, what would need to gate it. Was V4-scope in MECH-122's original 2026-03-23 registration notes; per 2026-08-01 governance correction, sleep (MECH-120/121/122/180 cluster) was pulled into V3 as necessary, so this entry is correctly V3-scoped despite the claim's own prose still reading V4 -- that prose is the stale artifact, not this entry's phase.

queue.title: MECH-122 content-packaging half: wire ThetaBuffer.consolidation_summary()/set_consolidation_mode() (existing V3 code, currently unwired) into run_sws_schema_pass()/force_cycle() so SWS writes to ContextMemory carry a spindle-analog content-selection signal proportional to novelty/MEL
queue.implementation_note: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-02 (/implement-substrate, IGW-20260801-197; ree-v3). ThetaBuffer.set_consolidation_mode()/consolidation_summary() (ree_core/latent/theta_buffer.py:146,159) are now called from run_sws_schema_pass() (ree_core/agent.py), gated by new REEConfig flags use_mech122_spindle_content_selection (default False, bit-identical off) and mech122_spindle_selection_gain (default 1.0). Each schema-installation prototype write is blended toward the theta-cycle consolidation reference in proportion to how CLOSELY it already matches it (habitual content homogenised, novel content keeps its own direction) -- giving ContextMemory's touched-slot diversity a channel to track novelty/MEL that a uniform per-write scale cannot (the diversity metric is cosine similarity of normalised rows, scale-invariant to a uniform multiplier). Deliberately distinct from the V3-EXQ-246 Phase-3 proxy (a single post-hoc write, measured zero effect): this modulates every schema-installation write in the pass itself. New contract probes in ree-v3/tests/test_flag_inertness.py: test_mech122_spindle_content_selection_fires_and_differentiates_writes (OFF-inert; ON in-range weight AND a different post-pass ContextMemory tensor than OFF on identical buffered content) and test_mech122_spindle_content_selection_gain_zero_collapses_to_off (gain=0.0 sanity check). VALIDATION RAN 2026-08-02/03 (V3-EXQ-861a): the mechanism DOES fire (mean_spindle_selection_applied=1.0), so the build is confirmed live/wired -- but its selection_weight is uniformly tiny/flat, tracing to ThetaBuffer.consolidation_summary() being self-referentially decoupled from the MEL/novelty axis (see failure_record). A second, independent DV (V3-EXQ-436c, slot_cosine_sim on SD-017/ARC-045/MECH-166) converges on a related write-path hypothesis (ContextMemory.write_gate bias-over-content collapse, untested by either run). STATUS implemented_validation_failed_needs_followup_fix: the original wiring gap this entry tracked is closed, but two new, more specific write-path defects are now the blocker -- see the two most recent failure_record entries for the exact follow-up fixes. FOLLOWUP FIX LANDED 2026-08-14 (chip-20260813-mech122-consolidation-ref-resource, session intelligent-elgamal-222d2b; ree-v3 6aa97ca): re-sourced the spindle content-selection novelty signal per the V3-EXQ-861a autopsy option (a). New REEConfig knob mech122_novelty_reference_mode (default 'mel_pe' when the master flag is on; 'recency' reproduces the legacy 861a path). In 'mel_pe' mode run_sws_schema_pass() additively lifts each prototype's per-prototype cosine novelty by the SD-MEL-CONSUMER relative-novelty gate MELConsumer.relative_novelty() = clamp(mel/ref-1, 0, 1) -- the SAME E3 prediction-error signal that drives MEL, calibrated against the driver's stable-base mel_reference (the arm-discriminating axis; V3-EXQ-701c showed it monotone in graded novelty). So the mean selection_weight now rises with the world_rule_shift/MEL axis (verified through the real pass: mean weight 0.001 at mel==ref -> 1.0 at mel=3*ref) instead of the flat ~0.004-0.01 861a produced. ThetaBuffer.consolidation_summary() is retained only as the homogenisation target (unchanged); theta_buffer.py is untouched. Default-OFF path bit-identical (whole block gated on use_mech122_spindle_content_selection); DV readout (mean_sws_new_slot_diversity) untouched -- the fix is upstream, in WHAT content is written. New contract probes in tests/test_flag_inertness.py: test_mech122_novelty_reference_mel_pe_tracks_mel_not_flat (mean weight DIFFERS across two novelty conditions AND legacy 'recency' is MEL-invariant), test_mech122_mel_relative_novelty_gate_semantics, test_mech122_novelty_reference_mode_is_wired_through_from_dims (3-site from_dims wiring guard). SCOPE: this closes ONLY the 861a self-referential novelty-reference defect (the blocker for MECH-180 DV3). The sibling V3-EXQ-436c write_gate bias-over-content write-path defect (third failure_record entry, slot_cosine_sim DV) is a DISTINCT open follow-up, NOT addressed here. Re-validation owed: re-run the 861-family driver (new letter) with use_mech122_spindle_content_selection=True and DV3 re-enabled -- separate /queue-experiment task (V3-EXQ-861b already covers DV1/DV2 with DV3 deliberately descoped for exactly this reason).

queue.implementation_hint: Lit-pull targeted_review_e1_forward_model_rollout_consistency (complete 2026-08-03) confirmed the collapse as a named, theorised failure family (anchors: PlaNet latent overshooting, DaD scheduled multi-step unrolling, TD-MPC multi-step latent consistency, Asadi direct sequence-conditioned model) but found a structural complication the original hint did not anticipate, verified in code: E1's transition is action-blind -- ree_core/predictors/e1_deep.py's forward() and predict_long_horizon() take no action parameter, and predict_long_horizon zeroes the z_self half of its LSTM input, so the action signal reaches z_world only through a squeezed second-order path via E2. All four literature fixes presuppose an action-conditioned transition and constrain how the predicted trajectory differs ACROSS actions -- exactly what C3's e1coe_score_var measures -- so 'add a multi-step/rollout-consistency term' alone would make E1's single trajectory more self-consistent without making the forty candidate action sequences any more distinguishable. The fix is likely an interface change (action-conditioning) plus an objective change, not an objective change alone. Review's provisional candidate ranking (Section 3): (1) TD-MPC-style multi-step latent consistency over an action-conditioned transition -- strongest template, additive to E1's existing training signal; (2) DaD scheduled multi-step unrolling -- cheapest, no architecture change, good first intervention but unlikely to fix C3 alone; (3) Asadi direct (state, action-sequence)->endpoint model -- best fit to what the evaluator actually consumes, held at 3 for the |A|^H generalisation question at horizon 30; (4) PlaNet latent overshooting -- grounded but NOT endorsed by its own ablation for a deterministic-LSTM architecture class like E1's, do not adopt by default; (5) contrastive next-state -- de-prioritised, no long-horizon anchor found, and the E2 review's contrastive recommendation does not transfer (it addresses single-step action identifiability, a different problem). This ranking is PROVISIONAL: node_class complex (probe-gated) is not yet discharged -- the review's Section 4 recommends a diagnostic probe (see depends_on_unresolved) to determine whether horizon-mismatch or action-blindness dominates the observed collapse before committing to an objective, since every ranked fix targets the former and presupposes the latter is solved.

A driver's own argparse default is the sole source of truth for how many seeds actually run, and validate_queue.py never cross-checks the declared count against either an explicit args --seeds list or the target script's own argparse default. Because validate() is already called from BOTH main() (the PreToolUse commit-blocking hook) AND experiment_runner.load_queue() (every runner's startup on every machine, sys.exit(1) on any error), this ONE check gives commit-time AND fleet-wide runner-startup enforcement -- including cloud workers that pull main directly and never see the commit hook -- without a second implementation. In infralimbic_avoidance_gate.py update_efficacy(): credit fires only when a directed action under threat DROPS z_harm_a (rare), while decay fires on every OTHER under-threat tick (common). Per-event rates are learn_rate=0.05 vs leak_rate=0.02, but the TICK-COUNT asymmetry (n_credit << n_decay) dominates, so the learned avoidance_efficacy underflows toward numerical zero in every run to date. Candidate fixes to probe: (a) credit-eligibility windowing so decay is not charged on every non-credit tick; (b) rebalance leak_rate vs learn_rate against realistic n_credit/n_decay ratios; (c) an eligibility trace with decay proportional to time-since-credit rather than per-tick.
